disclaimer: These scores are computed from the files shipped with this site. Active fire detections are thermal anomalies, not burned forest and not wildlife deaths. NDVI figures are a workbook, not a satellite extract. Habitat suitability is a resemblance to the occurrence table, not a sighting and not a forecast of movement. Neighbor counts are detections sitting in a shared airshed or on a known monsoon pathway. They are not a smoke forecast and not a health tally.

ndvi.note: Monthly NDVI means typed in as a workbook so the offline pipeline can run. They are not a NASA or MODIS download. Replace this file with statistics you extract yourself; the script only subtracts the two windows you give it.

neighbors.method: Count snapshot detections in West and Central Kalimantan (shared Borneo airshed) and, separately, those south of 1°N (a schematic southwest-monsoon pathway toward Singapore and Peninsular Malaysia). Not HYSPLIT. Not a forecast.

countries.why_it_can_be_large: Sarawak shares the island with West Kalimantan. In a dry season, smoke from peat fires has crossed that border and sat over inland towns for days.
Sabah sits on the same island airshed. Severe Borneo haze seasons have reached Malaysian Borneo, not only the peninsula.
Brunei is a small country wrapped by the Borneo airshed. When Kalimantan peat smolders, the smoke can arrive without a fire inside Brunei at all.
During the southwest monsoon, smoke from southern Kalimantan has crossed the sea and thickened the air over the peninsula. Schools and clinics have changed their day because of it.
Singapore has no forest fire of this kind, and still has haze advisories in severe seasons. The source can be hundreds of kilometres upwind.
